title: Trump Says He Will Endorse One Texas Senate Runoff Candidate and Expects the Other to Drop Out
description_short: Trump said he would soon endorse John Cornyn or Ken Paxton and expected the candidate he did not back to leave the Texas Republican Senate runoff.
description_medium: After John Cornyn and Ken Paxton advanced to a Republican U.S. Senate runoff in Texas, Trump said he would make an endorsement “soon” and expected the candidate he did not support to drop out. The Texas Tribune reported that Paxton later said he would stay in the race even if Trump endorsed against him. The account records Trump’s statement and Paxton’s response; it does not establish that Trump endorsed either candidate or that either withdrew.
description_long: After the March 3, 2026, Texas Republican primary, incumbent U.S. Sen. John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton advanced to a runoff. On March 4, President Donald Trump said he would make an endorsement “soon” and expected the candidate he did not support to drop out. The Texas Tribune reported that Paxton later said he would stay in the race even if Trump endorsed against him. It also said Trump had not yet weighed in on the contest, leaving an endorsement prospective at the time. Neither candidate had won the primary outright, so the runoff would decide the Republican nomination. This proposal records Trump’s stated intention and expectation, together with Paxton’s response. It does not say Trump had endorsed Cornyn or Paxton, that either candidate withdrew, or that his statement changed the runoff or its eventual result. The facts support a campaign statement in an election contest; they do not establish government action, an abuse of office, or a legal consequence.
